title: Marvin Penguin
text:
Welcome! I am an assistant professor of Computational Communication Science at the Boulders Beach Institute for Digital Communication, University of Cape Town.
My research uses computational methods to study how communities form, communicate, and navigate information environments online — drawing somewhat liberally on lessons from my own species. I am particularly interested in misinformation dynamics, online network formation, and what penguin colonies can teach us about echo chambers.
I am currently attending the Hacking Communication Science hackathon at ICA 2026 in Stellenbosch, South Africa.

title: Publications
text:
Penguin, M., & Albatross, A. (2024). Waddling Through the Twittersphere: Computational Analysis of Information Diffusion in Coastal Wildlife Communities. Journal of Computer-Mediated Communication, 29(3), 45–67. [DOI] [PDF] [Code]



Abstract

Using a computational approach to analyse 2.3 million posts, we examine how information spreads through online communities adjacent to wildlife conservation. Findings suggest that network topology in penguin-adjacent Twitter communities mirrors flocking patterns observed in physical colonies — with high clustering, rapid cascade formation, and susceptibility to coordinated misinformation. Implications for computational communication science and conservation communication are discussed.
Keywords: computational methods, information diffusion, wildlife communication, misinformation


Rockhopper, E., & Penguin, M. (2023). Fish or Fake News? Misinformation Sharing Patterns in Antarctic Online Communities. Political Communication, 40(2), 112–134. [DOI] [Preprint]


Abstract

This study examines misinformation sharing in online communities centred around Antarctic wildlife, using a mixed-methods approach combining automated content analysis with network mapping. We find that communities sharing misinformation about penguin conservation exhibit structural properties consistent with echo chambers, including low bridging capital and high internal density.
Keywords: misinformation, echo chambers, political communication, network analysis
